What's your favorite album, and why?

Botch - We Are The Romans (Mathcore / Metalcore) 1999

It is essentially everything I look for in music:

  1. Aggression
  2. Noise
  3. Experimentation

Couple that together with some genius songwriting and some of the most perfect melodic motives I've ever heard, you have a 10/10 album.
What in the fuck is "mathcore"? Do they yell out equations really loudly?
Metalcore with lots of dissonant, angular guitar riffs and odd time signatures. It sounds like spastic music to those who aren't used to it.

Metropolis Part 2: Scenes from a Memory - Dream Theater (Progressive Metal 1999)

This album has it all. Amazing story, technical playing, soft moments, hard moments, and everything else. It is the perfect album, and the bands magnum opus. It stands above my other favorites because it is a concept album with a story that could easily be in a movie or book.

Turnpike Troubadours - Diamonds & Gasoline

This shit on fleek

Hotel California - the Eagles

Just about every song is perfect. Concept albums are really a lost art, and this one is probably my favorite of all time. It wasn't my favorite until I listened to my dad's old vinyl copy.

"Wasted Time", "Hotel California", "Pretty Maids All in a Row", and "The Last Resort" are my favorite songs.

Yanni - Live at Acropolis. There are plenty of instrumental albums I listen to. In fact, the majority of what I listen to is instrumental. Vangelis, soundtracks by John Williams, classical music, you name it. But this one is special: It's so full of energy and life. Some may say it's cheesy or over-commercialized, but I like it as it is. Can listen to it anytime.

Gravity - John Mayer

[PTP] You wake up in a cabin... [Fun]
You wake up in a cabin, muddy and dirty. It's the middle of the night, so you're a bit frightened to take a step outside, hiding in the shelter of a raggedy old house.

Then you basically man the fuck up and rip your shirt open because you found and ingested some pills that were probably awesome. Labeled awesome. You roundhouse kick the door off the hinges in a perfect football-like spiraled arc and subsequently lands on another human. You run up to him, he had a gun and a letter with your name on it.

He screams. Too bad nobody will hear him. You've already succeeded in knocking him out after a 100x air-kick combo, and he may be dead. Maybe. That's too bad. You pick up the letter, and it says the following:

Jim,
I'll give you 5 cents if you give Phil this modded gun I made for him a few days ago. kthxbye!

Damn. Well, now I can take it off of his dead body.

The first thing you do is aim the gun at the dead body and fire it until the magazine is spent and there's a lot of blood. You're not sure why you just did that. Aren't you supposed to be awesome? You're questioning everything. Life. Religion. Love. Love? Your wife Stephanie! You need to call her to let her know that you're ok! You run back to the house and there's a painting of yourself on the wall in front of you. You didn't notice that before. You take the painting off the wall. There is a dildo and a letter with stephanie's name on it.

"Phil, I might leave the country because of you. Damn you! I know you'll try to follow me. The cops did nothing about you the first time. You delusional, sick bastard! I'm abandoning you in this forest, so I hope you die. There may be a few bears in there. Be careful. Love, Stephanie."

At this moment, questions really start rolling in. Was it smart to eat pills that i found? were they actually awesome? is this all a delusion caused by the pills as mentioned by stephanie or are the pills labeled as awesome so that i would take them and end the delusion?

And it's at that moment, with a very ornate and beautifully carved wooden dildo in one hand and a dull hunter's knife in the other, you begin to wonder how awesome the pills actually were. You'd like to contemplate more on where the letter you were sure you were reading went and why the inside of your house is painted very realistically like a forest but the sound of something growling coming from where you sure your kitchen was seems far too distracting...

The kitchen door slowly creaks open. Out steps a large ferocious bear, yet he seems strangely familiar. The bear is in torn blue jeans and wearing a ripped hat with the label "smokey" on it. Suddenly you think about how only you can prevent forest fires, but at the same time you need another dose of awesome to defeat this fire-prevention bear menace...

In a moment of haste you throw the ornate wooden dildo at his face and dash towards the spilled bottle of awesome pills and shove a handful in your mouth. Smokey wields the dildo in a fearsome manner and hurdles towards you with more speed than a raging forest fire, but you hold your ground with only the dull hunter's knife in hand.
You stab your awesome knife into its kidney, or at least where you think the bear's kidney was. But at that moment, you realize it was not a bear. It was the one and only...
Blake Anderson who was wearing his workaholics bear suit. your eyes go wide as he drops to his knees before you.

Then your start hyperventilating, and you realize that the awesome pills were just a placebo effect.... you're not as awesome as you thought. You wake up later, and it's bright as day outside. Well, because it's day, of course.

NASA is seriously considering "terraforming" part of the moon with robots

Hmm, no word yet on how they plan to transition from a crater that robots can operate in to one humanity can operate in.

It's still going to need a dome to maintain climate control, no matter how deep the crater is.

This article is pretty light on details, but other similar plans I have seen utilized caves or partially buried berm type dwellings near the crater walls. There is speculation that lava tubes might be accessible near those areas as well and would save having to excavate. The crater in question is too large for a dome to be practical with current technology. Covering a large fissure or canyon might be feasible, as is sometimes suggested for Mars.

This headline makes it sound like they are terraforming a part of the moon to have humans be able to stay there. While the grant seems to be more about setting up an interstellar gas station of sorts, and having MSL-class rovers (Curiosity size) doing surface experiments. Any way stage two funding isn't exactly huge, it is $500,000.

NASA is always up to cool shit.

I agree: Cool story, but the title is a bit click-baity.

TL;DR as I read it:

  1. Set up solar reflectors to redirect light into dark, scientifically promising craters

  2. Solar-powered rovers can explore said craters and conduct surface experiments

  3. ???

  4. Terraform
It would be cool to watch them with telescopes though.
